### Front line
According to the independent monitoring group DeepStateMap, 7.2 km² transitioned from contested to newly occupied territory, with Matiasheve in Donetsk Oblast recorded as 43% occupied. An additional 9.2 km² shifted to contested status, including portions of the village of Dobropillia (33% contested) and Novohryshyne (2% contested), while 0.1 km² returned to Ukrainian control.

In contrast, the Russian Ministry of Defence claimed extensive unverified territorial gains. Russian Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov and the Russian Defence Minister claimed Russian units completely captured Dobropillia (described by Russian sources as a city), as well as Pervomaiske and Serhiivka, while engaging in street fighting in Bilozerske. The Russian MoD additionally claimed units took control of Varvarovka and Mykolaivka in Kharkiv Oblast, claiming the total elimination of an encircled 2,000-strong Ukrainian grouping. In Zaporizhzhia and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, Russian commanders claimed capturing Malokaterynivka, Novopavlivka, Novoandriivka, and Velykomykhailivka, asserting vanguard forces advanced to within five kilometers of Zaporizhzhia city. Ukrainian sources and independent mappers did not confirm these sweeping Russian claims.

### Strikes and losses
*The Economist* war-fire model estimated six satellite fire detections classified as war-related (five in Khmelnytskyi Oblast and one in Zakarpattia Oblast).

Open-source video geolocated by GeoConfirmed showed fires at the Surgut oil refinery inside Russia following reported Ukrainian drone strikes, as well as a Russian Mi-28 helicopter targeted and likely hit by a Ukrainian drone. Across Ukraine, GeoConfirmed documented damage from reported Russian strikes: in Rivne, drones struck a logistics site, damaging cars, two retail supply stores, and a school; in Sumy, a strike damaged a shopping center, injuring three civilians; and further reported Russian strikes hit a civilian vehicle, injuring two, and a flea market, killing two civilians and injuring 19.

The Russian Ministry of Defence claimed its air defence forces intercepted 644 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight across numerous Russian regions, occupied Crimea, and the Black Sea, plus 47 additional drones during the day. The Russian MoD also claimed long-range drone strikes damaged logistics facilities in Teplodar (Odesa Oblast) and Rivne, struck two dry-cargo vessels bound for Odesa carrying alleged military cargo, and destroyed drone and missile depots in Kharkiv Oblast.

### Official statements
The Ministry of Defence of Ukraine announced government approval of an Engineering Defence Lines Equipment Strategy through 2028. Ukraine's Defence Minister stated the program establishes unified fortification standards, anti-drone protections, and digital monitoring to protect personnel and logistics. The Ukrainian MoD also released an upgraded 4,100-calorie field ration for frontline units and launched a tactical FPV drone countermeasure course on the Army+ mobile application.

The Russian Ministry of Defence reported that the Russian President visited a command post to receive operational briefings from the Chief of the General Staff, who claimed ongoing systematic strikes against Ukrainian defence production, transportation networks, and maritime logistics.
